conviction_note: This is the only name of the six with a real 8-K item 2.02 history, and its reaction distribution is genuinely fat on both sides (+16.3, +10.4, +7.2, +1.2, -2.5, -6.9, -13.3, -16.0; median 8.79%), so I size near a third of that and sign it negative: the stock closed above the 11-analyst consensus target, the street's FY27 EPS sits above the top of the company's own raised guidance, and the June re-rating that took it from $92 to a new high rested partly on a disclosed non-recurring gain - against which the company's own pattern of beating by 24-41% two quarters running is the honest counterweight and the reason the number is -3 and not -8.

findings.finding: SAIC went into the print trading above the sell side: the 2026-08-28 close of $125.96 is 3.5% above the $121.50 average target of 11 analysts polled by S&P Global, the consensus rating is Hold (2 Strong Buy / 8 Hold / 1 Strong Sell, unchanged since March), the single highest target is $137 and Goldman Sachs carries a Sell at $96 - and the street's FY27 modelled EPS of $10.18 is above the top of the company's own raised guidance of $9.90-$10.10 while modelled revenue of $7.19bn sits at the top of the $7.0-7.2bn guide.

findings.why_not_priced: The wire copy in this same capture says the opposite of what the numbers say: eight separate price-target raises after the Q1 'beat and raise' - Jefferies to $115 then $130, Truist to $110, JPMorgan to $125, UBS to $119, TD Cowen to $130, Citi to $132, Stifel to $137, Goldman to $96 - and every single non-Buy firm raised the target while maintaining Hold, Neutral or Sell. That is target-chasing, not conviction, and it leaves an average target below spot with zero rating upgrades in six months. The tape corroborates distribution rather than accumulation: on 2026-08-28, the last session before the print, SAIC printed a new 52-week high of $130.98 intraday, opened at $129.46 and closed at $125.96, down 2.33%, on 848,500 shares against a 406,645 twenty-day average. A market that had priced an in-line-with-guidance quarter as good news would not have rejected the new high on double volume the day before.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 beat that drove the +10.4% pop and the +37% re-rating from $92 was flattered by items the company itself identified as non-recurring: a $12 million gain from a venture investment's IPO that contributed 60 basis points to EBITDA margin and prompted the raise of full-year margin guidance to 10.1-10.3%, plus favourable timing of materials and an extension of the RITS program - while revenue guidance was left unchanged, organic growth was only 0.5%, and the lost RITS recompete is a stated $200 million revenue headwind in FY27.

findings.why_not_priced: The headline the market traded was 'SAIC Stock Rockets After Upbeat Q1' and 'Adj EPS $3.23 beats $2.29' - a 41% beat. The composition of that beat is in a trade-press body and in one line of a call summary, not in the wire item, and no preview in this capture mentions the venture gain. The full-year margin guide was raised on the back of a quarterly one-off, so an unchanged guide in Q2 is a de facto reduction against the street's $10.18, and the CFO scheduled exactly this quarter as the guidance re-look. If the market had discounted the one-off it would not have marked the shares up 37% in fifteen weeks to trade through the average target.

findings.finding: An 8-K carrying items 1.01, 2.03 and 9.01 - entry into a material definitive agreement plus creation of a direct financial obligation, event-dated 2026-08-14 - was accepted 2026-08-19T20:03:23Z, seventeen days before the print, and nothing in this 108-item capture covers it; it sits inside a three-week cluster with an item 5.02 8-K accepted 2026-08-10T11:00:07Z and two new Form 3s accepted 2026-08-20T20:28, while management runs a portfolio review and a $400m buyback programme.
findings.why_not_priced: The capture ran seven distinct queries including 'SAIC backlog book-to-bill fiscal 2027 guidance' and 'SAIC short interest price target' and returned 11 news items covering the earnings date, three contract awards, eight target changes and the 2026-08-28 dividend declaration - and not one word about a new financing agreement. New balance-sheet capacity taken on two weeks before results, in a company whose CEO said on the last call that they are 'exploring market opportunities aligned with their strategy' and reducing enterprise IT, plus two fresh Section 16 insiders and a third item-5.02 change in five months (2026-04-09, 2026-06-01, 2026-08-10), is the signature of a structural action being executed around the print. Be clear about the limit: item 2.03 also covers a routine revolver amendment, the body is not stored, and I therefore cannot sign this with any confidence - the small negative reflects that a leverage-increasing action at a 52-week high is more often a debit than a credit, not knowledge of what the agreement says.

baseline_tension: Cuts against the run-up: the baseline shows +7.5% over 20 days and only -2.3% from the 52-week high, and my findings say the bar has moved above both the sell-side target and the company's own guidance - but it also cuts against my own direction in one respect I will not hide, namely that SAIC has beaten consensus by 24% and 41% in its last two prints and both were rewarded with +16.3% and +10.4%, which is why the signed number is a third of the median move rather than the whole of it.
